sahneler.metin: A warehouse fire spread through downtown Boston.
Within hours, the flames destroyed the commercial district.
Many buildings had tall wooden mansard roofs.
Fire jumped easily from roof to roof.
An outbreak of horse flu had sickened the city's horses.
Fire engines had to be pulled by men.
Hydrants also had low water pressure.
Boston then improved its water supply and building codes.
